Let \(d\geq 3\) and \(k\geq 1\) be integers. A finite simplicial complex is a nonempty family of subsets of a finite set closed under taking subsets. Its vertices are the elements occurring in its faces, and its facets are its inclusion-maximal faces. It is pure of dimension \(e\) if every facet has cardinality \(e+1\). For a finite set \(W\), write \(2^W\) for the simplex consisting of all subsets of \(W\), allowing \(W=\varnothing\).

For a face \(\sigma\) of a complex \(\Delta\), define its deletion and link by
\[
\operatorname{del}_{\sigma}(\Delta)=\{G\in\Delta:\sigma\not\subseteq G\},\qquad
\operatorname{lk}_{\sigma}(\Delta)=\{G\in\Delta:G\cap\sigma=\varnothing,\ G\cup\sigma\in\Delta\}.
\]
A pure complex \(\Delta\) is called \(k\)-decomposable recursively if it is a simplex, or if it has a nonempty face \(\sigma\) with \(|\sigma|\leq k+1\) such that \(\operatorname{del}_{\sigma}(\Delta)\) is pure of the same dimension as \(\Delta\), and both \(\operatorname{del}_{\sigma}(\Delta)\) and \(\operatorname{lk}_{\sigma}(\Delta)\) are \(k\)-decomposable.

Define \(b(d,k)\) to be the least nonnegative integer \(r\) with the following property, and set \(b(d,k)=+\infty\) if no such integer exists. For every finite set \(V\) and every pure \(d\)-dimensional \(k\)-decomposable complex \(\Delta\) whose vertex set is exactly \(V\), there exist a set \(A\) disjoint from \(V\) with \(|A|=r\) and an ordering \(F_1,\ldots,F_t\) of all \((d+1)\)-element subsets of \(V\cup A\) that are not faces of \(\Delta\), such that every complex
\[
\Delta_i=\Delta\cup\bigcup_{j=1}^{i}2^{F_j},\qquad 0\leq i\leq t,
\]
is \(k\)-decomposable. Thus vertices in \(A\) enter only through added facets, and the final complex consists of all subsets of \(V\cup A\) of cardinality at most \(d+1\).

What is the exact value of \(b(d,k)\)?

The answer is The exact value is not established in general. The reported results give \(\max\{1,\min(d,k+1)-2\}\le b(d,k)\le d-2\), hence \(\boxed{b(3,k)=1}\) for every \(k\ge1\), and \(\boxed{b(d,k)=d-2}\) for \(k\ge d-1\).. This was proved recently, so it is not an open problem: your team's task is to prove it, completely, and to write Python that really computes or checks every step that can be checked. Printing what you believe is not evidence. Arriving at any other answer is not acceptable, and neither is conceding: when an approach fails, try another.

Proving these bounds takes two halves, for every \(d\ge3\) and \(k\ge1\): \(b(d,k)\le d-2\) (every pure \(d\)-dimensional \(k\)-decomposable complex on a finite vertex set \(V\) admits \(d-2\) new vertices and an ordering of all missing \((d+1)\)-element subsets such that adjoining their simplices one at a time leaves every intermediate complex \(k\)-decomposable), and \(b(d,k)\ge\max\{1,\min(d,k+1)-2\}\) (for every nonnegative integer \(r<\max\{1,\min(d,k+1)-2\}\), some such complex admits no set of \(r\) new vertices and no such ordering), yielding \(b(3,k)=1\) and \(b(d,k)=d-2\) when \(k\ge d-1\). from functools import lru_cache

@lru_cache(None)
def faces_of(F):
    return tuple(G for G in range(64) if G&F==G)
@lru_cache(None)
def dim(C):
    ff=[G for G in range(64) if C>>G&1]
    maximal=[G for G in ff if not any(G!=H and G&H==G for H in ff)]
    sizes={G.bit_count() for G in maximal}
    return sizes.pop()-1 if len(sizes)==1 else -99

    dimension=dim(C)
    if dimension==-99: return False
    ff=[G for G in range(64) if C>>G&1]
    if len(ff)==1<<(dimension+1): return True

def solve(n,timeout=60000):
    tris=list(combinations(range(n),3)); tindex={T:i for i,T in enumerate(tris)}
    Ts=[z3.Bool('t%d'%i) for i in range(len(tris))]
    facets=list(combinations(range(n),4));Fs=[z3.Bool('f%d'%i) for i in range(len(facets))]
    s=z3.Solver();s.set(timeout=timeout)
    for F,b in zip(facets,Fs):
        facebool=[Ts[tindex[T]] for T in combinations(F,3)]
        s.add(b==z3.And(facebool))
        s.add(z3.Sum([z3.If(q,1,0) for q in facebool])!=3)
    for T,b in zip(tris,Ts):s.add(z3.Implies(b,z3.Or([f for F,f in zip(facets,Fs) if set(T)<=set(F)])))
    for e in combinations(range(n),2):s.add(z3.Or([f for F,f in zip(facets,Fs) if set(e)<=set(F)]))
    nt=z3.Sum([z3.If(q,1,0) for q in Ts]);nf=z3.Sum([z3.If(q,1,0) for q in Fs])
    s.add(nt>=(n-2)**2,nf>=nt-(n*(n-1)//2-n+1),nf<len(facets))
